# Patches to the vendored my-3D2dge

The engine here is my-3D2dge v0.46.1 @ `cfa866aa45474868350cad1a7fc015e612f9305f` (see `VERSION.json`).

**Policy** (PLAN.md section 12):
- Extend first.
- Patch only where an extension would have to reach into private state.
- Mark each patch `// GTM-PATCH(n): <why>` in the code, and test it in `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs`.
- Each patch is written so it could be offered upstream. Record it here and in `PATCHES.json`; `tools/vendor-check.mjs`
  checks both.

| # | File | What | Why | Test | Upstream issue text |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (TileMap: `_isFront`, `queueWalls`, `_window`, `_boxCached`) | • `queueWalls` scans the cells under the screen (its corners taken to the ground through `view.toGround`, with room below for the tallest wall), not all w×h; the full scan stays for views with no inverse.<br>• A wall is kept while its top reaches the screen, however far below its foot is (the fixed 90-pixel margin dropped tall towers at the bottom edge).<br>• `map.cutAt(cx, cy, view)`: a game's own cut-away rule, consulted first by `_isFront` (true cuts, false keeps whole, null falls through to the engine's rule).<br>• A cached block checks its type, height and its neighbours' drawn heights instead of the map's version, so a cut that moves with the player re-bakes only the blocks it touches.<br>• A cut block's top shows the floor inside (`type.cutTop`, `type.cutRoof`) instead of the roof. | 25,600 cells were scanned every frame at 160×160. Tall walls popped in at the bottom edge. A player-relative cut-away needs a hook. | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` (the window loses no wall the full scan keeps, at 4 yaws × 3 zooms; tall walls; the hook; re-bakes) | "TileMap.queueWalls scans every cell of the map each frame and culls tall walls with a fixed 90-pixel margin. At city scale (160×160) the scan dominates, and towers pop in at the bottom edge. Proposal: scan the visible window (screen corners through toGround, plus the tallest wall's rise), cull by each wall's own height, and add a cutAt(cx, cy, view) hook so games can cut away by the player's position; a cut block's top may show the floor inside (cutTop)." |
| 2 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (TileMap: `_boxCached`, `_wcTrim`, `wallCache`, `prebakeWalls`) | • One wall-block cache for every view, bounded by pixels (`map.wallCacheMax`, 16M by default): the blocks used longest ago are dropped first, never one used this frame.<br>• Each block's image covers what it draws (its top, and the faces it shows down to each neighbour's height), not its whole prism: a roof cell inside a building is its top alone.<br>• `map.prebakeWalls(r, { margin, ms, view, at })`: bake the blocks about to scroll in (or those of a view about to be used: a zoom step, a turn) within a time budget.<br>• A cell's cut and whole blocks have their own slots, so a building the cut-away drops and restores bakes once each way.<br>• `map.wallCache()` reports `{ blocks, px, views }`. | The cache kept every block of the last four views: a long drive kept thousands. Fast cameras baked dozens of blocks in one frame (p99 21 ms at 300 u/s; 12.6-16.5 ms with prebaking). | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` (a long drive across three views stays under the budget, and nothing drawn this frame is dropped) | "TileMap's wall cache keeps every block of the last four views with no bound, and bakes synchronously as blocks enter. Proposal: one LRU bounded by pixels across views, block images cropped to the faces they draw, and a time-budgeted prebake for the margin around the screen or for the next zoom level." |
| 3 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (solids: `addSolids`, `_solidsNear`, `solidsNear`, `solidsMoved`; `collide`, `groundAt`, `heightAt`, `_liftSolids`) | • `map.solidsNear(x, y, r)`: the public query (a fresh array), for a game's own bodies (MOTOR's vehicles).<br>• `map.addSolids([{ id, x, y, z, o } \| { x, y, z, top, hx, hy, c, s }])`: many solids with one `version` bump; ready boxes (deck slabs, pillars) need no shape.<br>• A 64-unit bucket grid over the solids, rebuilt when `map.solids` is replaced, changes length or the version moves (`solidsMoved()` after moving one in place). `collide`, `groundAt`, `heightAt` and the render lift look only at nearby solids, in `map.solids` order, so results are identical to the full scan. Below 24 solids the full list is used. | Street furniture and deck pillars are hundreds of solids, checked by every body, every query and every queued drawing; each `solid()` call bumped the version, re-keying caches. | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` (3,000 random queries against 600 turned solids match the full scan exactly; addSolids) | "map.solid bumps the version per call and the solid checks loop over every solid for every body and query. Proposal: a bulk addSolids with one version bump, and a bucket grid for collide/groundAt/heightAt/_liftSolids that visits candidates in array order (identical results)." |
| 4 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (Input: the constructor, listeners, `press`, `clear`, `tick`) | `input.raw = { keys, pads, active, activity }`:<br>• every key code held, bound or not;<br>• every connected pad's buttons as `{ pressed, value }`, plus its axes;<br>• the active pad, which is the last one used;<br>• an activity clock: keys, mouse move, click, wheel, touch, pad buttons, sticks past the dead zone, triggers;<br>• `raw.pressed`: the codes pressed since the step before, so a tap shorter than a step still counts once.<br><br>The engine's own pad is now the active one, not the first connected. | Analog triggers for driving. A DualSense that isn't pad 0. An idle timer for attract modes. Game-owned per-context bindings that never call `use()`, which clears held buttons. | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` | "Input: expose raw device state and an activity clock. `anyPressed()` sees only bound actions, `tick()` reads only the first pad's `pressed` flags, and nothing records the time of the last input of any kind. Games need these for attract modes, analog triggers and their own binding layers." |
| 5 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (Audio: `bus`) | `audio.bus(name)`: the gain node of the `'sfx'`, `'music'` or `'master'` bus (made with the context at the first sound; null without Web Audio). | MOTOR's sequencer (the radio, a mission's score) and its continuous voices (engines, sirens, rain) must play through the engine's buses so the master volume, the effects and music levels, mute and the ducking hold for them, without reaching for `_sfxBus`. | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` (the buses are the ones the engine's own sounds and music play through; the levels and mute reach a voice connected to them) | "Audio: a game that makes its own voices (a sequencer, an engine hum) can't route them through the engine's buses, so the volume settings, mute and ducking don't reach them. Proposal: a public audio.bus('sfx' | 'music' | 'master') getter." |
| 7 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (Lighting: `render`) | • `lights.res = 2` (or 3, 4): the light field is worked out on a grid that much coarser and the dark and the lights' colours are scaled up smoothly over the frame; 1, the default, is the engine's own, pixel for pixel.<br>• The tint's saturation curve comes from a 1,025-entry table made once per tint, not `Math.exp` three times for every lit pixel of every frame (the same steps of 8). | Lowtown at night in ISO: `lights.render` cost 8.2 ms a frame with about 30 street lamps of radius 88 (the curve alone 17% of the frame); 4.4 ms with the table, 1.3 ms with `res = 2`. | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` (the coarse field matches the full one at each cell's centre; the table is the curve, step for step) | "Canvas lighting costs a few ms per frame with many lights: every light walks its bounding box per pixel, and the tint curve calls Math.exp three times per lit pixel. Proposal: a lights.res option that computes the field on a coarser grid and scales it up smoothly, and a lookup table for the tint curve." |
| 8 | `engine/my-3d2dge.js` (Humanoid: `_drawHD`, `_drawClassic`, `_weaponApi`) | `o.weaponDraw(api)`: when a rig has it, the rig calls it where it would draw its own weapon and skips the built-in gun, staff or sword. `api` = `{ g, P(p, df, dr, dz), J, Q, u, view, rig, classic, push(depth, fn) }`: a rig-local point to the screen (the rig's own projection, squash, spin and 3/4 cheat included), the joints, the pixels a unit, and `push`, which draws `fn` at a depth among the limbs (a gun held on the far side is behind the body). `o.weapon` still sets the pose ('gun' points, 'sword' swings). | The engine has one weapon model a kind (a pistol, a sword, a staff); a game with eleven weapons (shotguns, a rocket tube, a bat) has to draw its own. Drawing over the rig afterwards can't put a gun behind the arm that holds it, and would mean copying the rig's private projection (`_cheat`, `sq`). | `tests/unit/engine-patches.test.mjs` (both styles: the hook replaces the built-in model; `P` of a joint is the joint on screen; parts pushed far and near draw first and last) | "Humanoid draws three built-in weapons only. Proposal: a weaponDraw(api) hook, given the rig's projection and a depth-sorted push, so games can draw any held model in place of the built-in one, sorted with the limbs." |

6 (a `floor: false` flag) stays unneeded while the city never calls `drawFloor`. 7 was not in the plan: DECISIONS D11; nor was 8: DECISIONS D14.
